title: FloodGuard Policy Renewal: New Term and Term Premium
content:
A FloodGuard Private Flood Policy renews for a new twelve-month term with continuous coverage. At renewal the policy takes on the new term's start date, its end date and the renewal term premium, which is the annual premium of the new term, excluding the policy fee, after the renewal rate cap.

## When the renewal term premium is fixed

The renewal term premium is fixed only after the indicated premium for the upcoming term stands on the policy.

Put the other way round: while the policy shows no indicated renewal premium for the upcoming term, no renewal term premium is fixed for it.

## Renewing the policy

Capability. Renewing writes the new term onto one FloodGuard flood policy. The policy's term start, term end and annual term premium are replaced with the new term's values, and the indicated renewal premium on the policy is cleared. Two charges are posted to the policy's premium account for the new term:

- the premium charge for the new term, posted as installment 1, due on the new term's start date and billed to the named payer; and
- the annual policy fee for the new term.

The policy then shows the new term, and its premium account shows both new charges.

How it is invoked. The tool is `renew_flood_policy_8cc307a9`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it on the verified caller's FloodGuard policy.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format and values |
|---|---|---|
| `flood_policy_id` | The reference number of the FloodGuard flood policy record being renewed, as returned by the flood policy lookup for the verified caller. | Identifier exactly as the lookup returns it. |
| `new_effective_date` | The start date of the new term. | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `new_expiration_date` | The end date of the new term. | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `term_premium` | The annual premium of the new term, excluding the policy fee. | USD as a plain number with 2 decimal places; stored rounded half-up to 2 decimal places. |
| `policy_fee` | The annual policy fee charged for the new term. | USD as a plain number with 2 decimal places; stored rounded half-up to 2 decimal places. |
| `payer` | Who the new term's premium charge is billed to. | One of `insured`, `mortgagee`, `none`. |

The values of `payer`:

- `insured` — the named insured pays the premium directly (annual or two-pay billing);
- `mortgagee` — the premium is paid from the lender's escrow account (mortgagee escrow billing);
- `none` — the charge is billed to nobody in particular and no payer is named.

### Receipt

A successful call returns a dictionary rendered as text with: `flood_policy_id` (the policy renewed); `effective_date` and `expiration_date` (the new term, YYYY-MM-DD); `term_premium` (USD with 2 decimal places); `premium_charge_id` and `fee_charge_id` (the reference numbers of the two premium account entries posted); and `status`, which reads `policy_renewed`, meaning the renewal was written.

## Hypothetical illustration

A policy whose term ends on 2026-06-01, renewed with `new_effective_date` 2026-06-01, `new_expiration_date` 2027-06-01, `term_premium` 920.00, `policy_fee` 50.00 and `payer` `mortgagee`, afterwards shows the term 2026-06-01 to 2027-06-01 with a term premium of 920.00 and no indicated renewal premium; its premium account shows a premium charge of 920.00 for the new term, due 2026-06-01 and billed to the mortgagee, and a policy fee charge of 50.00. The figures are hypothetical.
